subject: Post-call: HealthBridge data territory binding vs multi-region fallback
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Cheng <laura.cheng@healthbridge.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2024 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call: HealthBridge data territory binding vs multi-region fallback

Hi Laura — great talk earlier today. Thanks for walking through the HealthBridge ingestion patterns and compliance constraints. Quick recap and the open items we said we'd follow up on: 

Summary:
- Primary ask: ensure customer PII (name, DOB, MRN) is always stored and processed in the customer-designated territory (US-East) when originating from US apps.
- Secondary: acceptable cross-region failover behavior during outage windows (max RTO 6 hours).
- Backup/restore: HealthBridge needs encrypted backups with explicit region-of-origin tags and a documented restore path that does not replicate backups automatically outside the pinned region.

Open questions for Redwood team (what we'll answer in follow-ups):
1) Can we pin at the project/tenant level vs only account-wide?
2) During failover, can we keep logs and KV cache metadata bounded to the region or must some logs be routed to the recovery region?
3) Retention: HealthBridge wants configurable retention at the table/collection level, including short-term PII purge options (90/180/365 days).

Next steps from our side: I'll pull together a short compare sheet (pinning modes + failover tradeoffs) and attach the draft. Also will confirm behavioral guarantees (RTO/RPO) per capacity tier.

Attachments: hb-region-options-summary.xlsx (draft), redwood-pin-options.md (explainers)

Would you prefer a written decision matrix or a short follow-up call to walk the team through tradeoffs?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Cheng <laura.cheng@healthbridge.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@healthbridge.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2024 20:40:12 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: HealthBridge data territory binding vs multi-region fallback

Aditya — thanks for the summary, that looks good. A few clarifying items from our side before we decide on next steps: 

1) Pin scope: health IT wants control at the application (project) level because we run multiple regulated apps under the same account. Account-level pinning won't work for us. Can Redwood support per-project pinning or a tagging policy that enforces region binding?

2) Failover constraints: Our legal team requires that logs containing PII identifiers never be replicated to outside the pinned territory except to a dedicated, encrypted legal escrow during subpoena scenarios. Operational logs without identifiers are fine to replicate. Can you explain how Redwood separates application logs vs operational telemetry and whether that separation is configurable?

3) Backups: we need a manual approval step before backups are restored to an alternate region. Automatic cross-region replication of backups is a blocker. Is that behavior configurable?

4) Retention & purge: We have a short-term purge requirement for a subset of PII (90 days). Need confirmation on whether Redwood can trigger selective purge requests for customer-scoped data and whether there's an audit trail for those purges.

If you can answer those in writing we'd share with Legal and Security; otherwise happy to block 30 minutes Thursday morning for a quick walkthrough.

Best,
Laura Cheng
Head of Infrastructure & Security
HealthBridge

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Cheng <laura.cheng@healthbridge.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, legal@healthbridge.com
Date: Wed, 17 Apr 2024 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: HealthBridge data territory binding vs multi-region fallback

Laura — appreciate the specific asks, answers below and a proposed next step. Short answers first: yes (per-project pinning), yes (log separation/enforcement), yes (manual-approval for cross-region restore), yes (selective purge + audit trail). Details: 

1) Per-project pinning: Redwood supports pinning at the project/tenant level. We implement this via a region-affinity rule attached to the project config; requests and persistent artifacts (storage, KV cache, backups) are tagged with a region_id and routing enforces that reads/writes are served from pinned infra unless an approved failover is triggered. See attached draft (redwood-pin-options.md) for policy examples.

2) Log separation: We separate application-level request logs (which may contain identifiers) from operational telemetry (metrics, runtime traces) at ingestion. Application logs are stored in the same pinned region by default and can be configured to be accessible only to roles you approve. Operational telemetry is routed to a central observability plane and can be redacted/aggregated before leaving the pinned region. We can provide a whitepaper and a config checklist for the specific log classes you want kept in-region.

3) Backups & restore: Automatic cross-region backup replication is optional — we can disable replication and require manual export + restore approval for any restore executed outside the pinned region. Backups carry a region tag and an access policy that requires an explicit restore justification and an admin approval flow (audit events logged).

4) Retention & selective purge: We support retention policies per-collection and on-demand purge APIs that return an audit token. Purge operations are asynchronous; Redwood will provide an immutable audit record (who/when/selector) and a signed confirmation once the purge completes. We can align the retention windows to 90/180/365 days as requested.

Next steps: 
- I'll attach the one-pager and a proposed decision matrix for per-project pin options (see attachments).
- If Legal wants more, Ben can follow up with the SOC2 and controls mapping doc; Monica and I will schedule a config walkthrough next week.

Proposing: 30 min on Thu 18 Apr 2024 15:00 ET (11:00 PT) to run through tradeoffs and confirm the exact policy defaults you want. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: hb-region-options-summary.xlsx, redwood-pin-options.md
